title: Special Projects
description:

The Principal runs a global portfolio spanning investments, operating companies, and new ventures. This role is a unique opportunity to work directly with the founder across all areas of build: problems that are high-stakes, largely undefined, and require someone who can take full ownership and see them through.
The Requirement
You will work directly with the founder to deliver structured action that turns complex situations and ideas into clear decisions and outcomes. The measure of success is whether the objective gets done, and done well.
The work crosses domains constantly; there will be projects across a variety of expertise areas, many of them unfamiliar. You are expected to own things end to end: from figuring out what the problem actually is, to building the answer, to seeing it through. You do not hand things off.
Applicants of diverse backgrounds are encouraged to apply. We are less interested in your background than in what you’ve actually done and how you think.

The scope is broad and will evolve with the needs of the Principal. Past and current work has spanned startup incubation, acquisitions and acqui-hires, AI initiatives, real estate, data infrastructure, hiring, and philanthropic work, among other things.
What connects these is not the domain but the level of ownership required and the stakes involved. You will be expected to operate with full discretion and move fluidly across changing priorities.
The Incentive
We believe in aligned incentives. Your compensation will be structured so that if you deliver outsized value and solve high-leverage problems, you will participate in the upside.
To Apply
Send a brief note on a complex problem you solved simply because you refused to let it fail.

title: Freshwater Strategy Director, Asia Pacific
description:
What We Can Achieve Together:
Freshwater ecosystems around the world are in crisis - pushed to the brink by the climate crisis - resulting in a sharp and long-term decline in water security and biodiversity. Freshwater is central to The Nature Conservancy's 2030 Goals, and to our work in Asia Pacific. At TNC we have set ourselves three ambitious goals to achieve by 2030: Safeguard or restore at least 1 million kilometers of healthy rivers and streams, conserve 30 million hectares of lakes, wetlands, deltas and floodplains, and ensure over 10 million people benefit directly from healthy freshwater ecosystems. Asia Pacific will make a critical contribution to these organizational goals.
Asia Pacific holds significant water resources vital for people and natural ecosystems, and hosts unique freshwater biodiversity that requires urgent action and integrated management approaches. The Nature Conservancy works with a wide range of partners to make transformational changes, orchestrate system-wide approaches, conserve freshwater biodiversity at scale and align investments with the natural infrastructure that underlies water security. Managing water is crucial for sustained economic growth, and to avoid conflicts among water users. Nature's role in water regulation is technically well-understood but vastly underrepresented in spending.
We’re Looking for You:
The Nature Conservancy seeks an innovative leader with deep expertise in freshwater science, biodiversity conservation and/or water resource management to serve as the Freshwater Strategy Director for Asia Pacific. The Freshwater Strategy Director works for the Asia Pacific regional program to develop and support freshwater conservation strategies across the region in close partnership with TNC country and global programs. The Freshwater Strategy Director ensures TNC has an impactful portfolio of freshwater conservation projects in Asia Pacific for resilient watersheds and durable freshwater protection, enhancing, scaling, and innovating from significant existing programs within the region and across the globe. They report to the Asia Pacific Deputy Director of Conservation, but must function well in a decentralized and highly matrixed structure.
ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS & RESPONSIBILITIES
In close collaboration with the Asia Pacific Lead Scientist & Director of Conservation, staff in Country programs, and TNC Global teams, the Asia Pacific Director of Freshwater Conservation designs and supports the implementation of freshwater conservation strategies in the Asia Pacific. This includes both nature-based solutions for water provisioning and regulation, and durable freshwater protection.
They cultivate collaborative working partnerships with the Asia Pacific regional country teams and with other staff across the Conservancy and external partners to increase the pace, scale and impact of our conservation strategies. This includes aligning our work in Asia Pacific with TNC’s global teams and pathways of impact.
They improve freshwater conservation outcomes through supporting and building scientific and technical capacity with country programs in the Asia Pacific. And through refining and strengthening our Theories of Change for freshwater conservation.
They help negotiate innovative solutions with diverse stakeholders, including local communities, government agencies, corporations, and lending institutions.
They ensure freshwater conservation work across the Asia Pacific Region is strongly represented in Asia Pacific’s Portfolio Management approach, and is underpinned by robust monitoring, evaluation and learning programs that report on progress against TNC’s 2030 Goals
They are the focal point in Asia Pacific for TNC’s Nature4Water partnership.
They work closely with regional and global fundraising teams to actively pursue and secure fundraising opportunities that advance freshwater priorities - including TNC’s Forever Freshwater priority geographies in Mongolia and Australia - for Asia

GiveDirectly has delivered more than $1B in cash directly to 2+ million people living in poverty across 15 countries since 2011. We believe cash transfers are one of the most scalable, cost-effective, and dignified forms of aid, with the research to back it up. Our work has been covered by The Economist, NPR, TED, and The Washington Post. We are one of Time100’s Most Influential Companies of 2026.

Our culture is candid, analytical, and non-hierarchical. We support high ownership and real professional growth. Curious about what it's really like to work here? Read our values and hear from the people who do. If they resonate, this could be a great fit!

Job Type: Full-time
Location: This role is fully remote but must be based in Mozambique or DRC only.
Priority Application Deadline: October 5, 2026 or until we receive a critical mass of applications
About this role
GiveDirectly is planning to grow delivery roughly tenfold by 2028. Getting there means changing our programs faster and more often than we ever have: consolidating country programs onto a small number of common Salesforce builds through 2027, then layering on new enrollment models - large-group barazas, remote and self-enrollment - from 2028.
Every one of those changes has to land with roughly 650 people in country operations. A new survey design is only as good as the Field Officer's understanding of it at seven in the morning, standing in a village with a tablet and no supervisor nearby. A Country Director needs to know why we changed something and what risk it carries. A Field Manager needs to know what changes about supervision and quality checks. A Field Officer needs to know exactly what to do differently tomorrow, and nothing else.
That translation work is this role. You will turn new survey designs, program changes, and system releases into training materials, live training sessions, demo videos, release notes, and internal communications pitched at the right level for each audience - from Country Director down to Field Officer.
We are looking specifically for someone who has been a Field Officer, or held a directly equivalent frontline role. Not as a nice-to-have: this role exists because materials written by people who have never run a registration are consistently too abstract, too long, and wrong about which details actually matter. You should know from experience what makes a training useful and what makes it a waste of a morning.
Your work will be anchored on the 2027 rollout - supporting the consolidation of country programs onto common Salesforce builds, which is high-volume and has real deadlines - and will absorb 2028 pilot material as those designs become real. Beyond that, you will be a genuinely useful pair of hands to a small, fast-moving product team: expect a meaningful share of your time to go to ad-hoc support that doesn't fit neatly in a job description.
We work across English, Portuguese and French. Materials that only exist in English do not reach Mozambique or DRC, and translating them after the fact is slow and lossy. We need someone who can write well in English and work in at least one of Portuguese or French.
Explicitly not in scope:

• Designing the programs or surveys themselves - owned by the 2028 Design Lead, the STPM, Large Transfers, and the Senior Director, Product; this role makes those designs usable, and will often be the first person to notice when a design isn't explainable

• Salesforce configuration and technical build work - owned by the Technical Program Managers

• Deciding which change requests get built and when - owned by the STPM, Large Transfers

• Staff development, onboarding, and performance training - owned by the People team; this role covers product and program training only
